Responsibility: 1. Information for the Use of Others

Prepares program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives; monitors and assesses management accountability for departmental programs; and recommends ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations.

Collects and analyzes foundation data in order to create new information about programs and their effectiveness; selects data sources to be used; develops and gathers information which will be used by management to make informed decisions concerning the scope, structure, redefinition or termination of major programs, initiatives, operations or activities.

Develops methodologies, tools and techniques to support the evolution of and use of professional practices and government-wide standards for the conduct of evaluation and review activities. This information is shared with colleagues, Senior Management, Central Agencies, OGDs, and other professional and governmental organizations.

Provides the Planning and Evaluation Manager with critical information for the development, use and maintenance of various system applications such as the LTP database, Risk Profile and the Management Accountability Framework which will significantly influence all aspects of systems development, implementation, maintenance and use.

Reviews emerging issues, trends and developments impacting government operations (i.e., strategic planning processes, performance evaluations, program evaluations and program review ) in order to develop and recommend strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives. 2. Well-Being of Individuals No specific requirement

3. Leadership of Human Resources Plans, organizes and coordinates the work of project teams involved in the conduct of special studies, surveys and projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, participates in the recruitment of staff, provides input to employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

4. Money A. PLANNING AND CONTROLLING: Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets.

B. ACQUIRING FUNDS: No specific requirement C. SPENDING FUNDS: Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated. 5. Physical Assets and Products Ensures custody of, and protect confidential, secret and top-secret documents as well as proprietary and commercially confidential documents. This information is used to undertake evaluations and reviews. Often these documents are highly sensitive and cannot be copied. These documents usually cannot be replaced without substantial effort.

Creates, maintains and has custody of active hard copy and electronic project working files and Senior Management performance reviews and evaluations. These contain evidence (specimens, analysis-documentation, project findings, conclusions and recommendations) gathered during the course of evaluations and reviews. In many instances they are the Department’s only official record and depository of project results. Project team members use the working paper files to perform their work in delivering the evaluation-review services to departmental Senior Management and stakeholders. If lost, some documentation could be replicated or reconstructed from other sources, while other documentation would extremely be difficult to replace.
6. Ensuring Compliance Liaises with the Industry Portfolio Office and the Treasury Board Secretariat on an ongoing basis to ensure compliance to established standards.
Skills: 7. Job Content Knowledge Application Knowledge of statistical methods and techniques to conduct research and analysis into economic trends, policy and initiative issues; to collect and analyze foundation data in order to create new information about programs and their effectiveness; to select data sources to be used; and to develop and gather information which will be used by management to make informed decisions concerning the scope, structure, redefinition or termination of major programs, initiatives, operations or activities.
Knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques to develop evaluation standards and performance indicators as well as procedures for monitoring and reporting purposes.

Knowledge is required of computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results, including specialized software such as statistical sampling, computer assisted techniques, automated working papers, and flowcharting.

Knowledge of social science research methods, techniques and practices, including multi-disciplinary analysis methods, to carry out analysis on a variety of approaches regarding performance and accountability framework in other levels of government, other jurisdictions and in the private sector.

Skill in synthesising information from diverse disciplines (management science, economics, and public policy administration, etc.) to facilitate the development and the implementation of interdepartmental performance frameworks. Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of consultation, management, conflict resolution, small group process, interviewing and counselling to lead project teams, to negotiate contracts for services and agreements with other institutions. 8. Contextual Knowledge A. OWN WORK UNIT: Knowledge is required of the organization and objectives of the evaluation division; the strategic direction, culture, structure and organization, mandate, objectives, policies, procedures and work tools of the Field, branch, division; and the structure and organization of project work teams, their mandates and objectives. This knowledge is required to achieve operational objectives and results in an effective and efficient manner, and to recommend new or improved business services, policies, systems and procedures. Knowledge of the policies, procedures, guidelines, mandate and personnel of the Branch to provide consultative services related to strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting; and to develop and recommend strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives. B. OWN DEPARTMENT OR AGENCY: Knowledge of the policies, procedures, guidelines, mandate and personnel of the department to prepare program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives; to monitor and assess management accountability for departmental programs; and to recommend ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations. C. OTHER FEDERAL DEPARTMENTS AND AGENCIES: Knowledge of the personnel, organization, priorities, policies, mandate, objectives, goals and programs of a wide range of client departments and organizations to provide advice and guidance regarding the development and implementation of reporting and performance review frameworks, processes and tools.

Knowledge is required of the Parliamentary system and machinery of government, and its expectations for the Department, policy making and legislative processes, government priorities, and current and emerging management issues; the mandate, policies, programs, operations and reporting processes of Parliamentary committees, central agencies, and other federal government departments; and the role of Treasury Board and the Privy Council Office.

D. CANADIAN PRIVATE SECTOR AND OTHER PUBLIC SECTORS: Knowledge of personnel and organisation of different orders of government (provincial, territorial, municipal), the academic community, and non-government organisations in order to effectively communicate on performance and accountability approaches, methods, theories, studies, and analysis for the purpose of strengthening performance reporting to Parliament and the public. Knowledge of think tanks that are working in the area of citizen engagement, societal indicators and quality of life modelling, to carry out analysis regarding alternative performance and accountability frameworks and approaches (e.g. National Statistical Council). E. INTERNATIONAL PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTOR: Knowledge of personnel and organisation of different national governments, international organisations (International Statistical Agencies), the international academic community, and non-government organisations in order to effectively communicate on performance and accountability approaches, methods, theories, studies, and analysis for the purpose of strengthening performance reporting to Parliament and the public. F. LEGISLATION AND REGULATIONS: Knowledge of certain sections of legislation related to client departments and to STC reporting and reviews regulations and requirements. This knowledge is required to handle and process sensitive information and documentation related to client departments and reporting processes.

9. Communication A. COMMUNICATION IN: Listening and evaluation skills to interpret verbal and non-verbal communication when receiving information and feedback from colleagues, managers and departments to determine what their concerns are, to retain salient points and synthesize information on a variety of issues of differing complexity, and to understand opinion and points of view. Reading and listening skills, to maintain knowledge of key developments, research and innovations related to reporting and accountability processes and techniques, to attend conferences and meetings of professional associations related to auditing, financial analysis, and accountability reporting, to analyse and assess a wide range of alternative accountability approaches, strategies and processes, to liase and consult with academics, researchers and related specialists regarding a wide range of issues and innovations. B. COMMUNICATION OUT: Oral and written skills to make presentations and to consult with managers from client departments and organizations regarding strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting.
Writing skills to prepare program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives.

Speaking and writing skills are required to explain and clarify issues, to present arguments, report findings and recommendations to senior officials and stakeholders, and to adapt large volumes of information and specialized terminology in order to improve departmental policies, programs and operations.

10. Motor and Sensory Skills Dexterity and co-ordination skills are required on a daily basis to operate a computer keyboard and mouse to search, retrieve, and manipulate and transform information and data from information bases, the Internet and Intranet as well as to type briefing notes, memoranda, notes, reports, and analytical documents. Any requirement for proficiency, precision and speed in the conduct of this activity is under the control of the incumbent.
Effort: 11. Intellectual Effort Researches and analyzes complex, multi-dimensional and interrelated variables and issues; assesses the range of socio-economic and/or environmental impacts; and presents options and recommendations based on conclusions.

Develops new tools for statistical analysis in response to unique problems. The areas under evaluation are highly sensitive and require solid proof of findings. Views of stakeholders with differing or conflicting views must be integrated into the analyses, adding to the level of effort required. Additional constraints that hamper the analysis include information gaps that require the development and use of proxy measures.

Develops and carries out analytical reviews; develops strategic recommendations and proposals; and writes reports, working papers, background and briefing material for the direct use of analysts and senior officials in the directorate. Defends the results of analysis of complex issues and of information drawn from a wide variety of sources with varying degrees of technical complexity. The challenge lies in the lack of data and information or lack of existing tools or frameworks of analysis, which address the multiple objectives that departments and the government have in terms of accountability and reporting to Parliament. 12. Sustained Attention Attention is required to analyse complex issues and interpret and understand them in order to develop papers, briefings and recommendations. Participating in meetings with colleagues, senior management, or officials from other departments over periods of one to three hours requires sustained auditory and visual attention to focus in order to understand policy discussions and to be able to make effective contributions. 13. Psychological/Emotional Effort Psychological/emotional efforts are required on an ongoing basis to maintain professionalism when dealing with politically sensitive issues, adapting to shifting priorities and imposed short deadlines to meet the multiple, competing and sometimes conflicting demands of management. There is little or no control over the occurrence, frequency and duration of such situations. Psychological and emotional effort is required to maintain composure and professionalism in working with teams, meeting tight project deadlines, negotiating and consulting with TBS and IPO and providing constructive feedback to processes and methodologies. There is limited control over the occurrence, frequency and duration of these situations.
Urgent high profile evaluations requested by the Minister, Deputy Minister, or Senior Managers can cause immediate changes to existing assignments and priorities.
